I participated in the recount for a couple days as an observer.

When a precinct is going to be recounted, they first check that the bag of ballots shows no sign of tampering and that the seal number on the bag matches the poll book. Once the bag is opened, they do a recount by hand of the physical number of ballots. If that number does not match the number of ballots in the poll book then that precinct is not recounted and the previous results stand. They have three chances to do this initial count.

An election official has to announce whether a precinct Can be recounted at this point. I estimate that 10 to 15% of precincts could not be counted where I was (not Detroit).

I was surprised at the number of ballots that were either not counted correctly during election night or during the recount, based on what I saw. It was about 1 every 1,500 ballot. But this is due to random errors that would cut both ways and should not have affected the outcome. The allegation for Detroit is deliberate errors, which is belivable.

Unofficially, Hillary Clinton picked up a net of about 60 votes in Michigan at the time the recount was called off. However, I think that number would have dropped as the precincts that were counted were heavily Democratic and the precincts that were not counted leaned Trump.

While I agree that extreme far-right opinions dominate the speech on voat, I am not entirely convinced it is a deliberate and malicious plot.

There are indeed powerful propaganda machines active on all sides of any spectrum you'd like classify opinions on, but you forget one powerful force in human nature. We like to be right, and we don't like to be wrong. On top of that, we prefer to associate with people similar to us and we despise the outgroup with a burning passion.

This is why echo chambers are everywhere on the internet, and a true free marketplace of ideas is mostly an idealized fiction. People self-organize around ideas they agree with and will antagonize anyone who disagrees with their core values. You see it as the Reddit hivemind, the monotony and repetitivity of a facebook wall. New people with differing opinions often feel unwelcome on established fora and tend not to stick around too long.

The only way to truly inform yourself is to visit groups of people who disagree with you and listen. Don't dismiss their opinion out of hand. This is one of the hardest thing to do, to allow yourself to hear something the deepest core of yourself finds revolting and actually keep listening to it. An even better, but even more difficult excercise is to try to argue against your own core values. Have you ever tried it? It's dizzying.

But if you do that, you will refine your worldview. You will have to drop some assumptions you had because they have become untenable. You will have strengthened other opinions you hold because you find they are well-established and rooted in fact. It is the only way to truly learn, instead of spiraling endlessly in your own self-congratulatory echo chambers.
